scenario.draft: Test pagination, searching, and filtering configuration records. Set up multiple configurations with different keys and descriptions using the POST /discussionboard/configurations endpoint. Send filter requests by key, description substrings, or pagination parameters. Verify paginated metadata and content match query. Confirm a 400 error on invalid filter structure or out-of-range pagination values (e.g., negative page/limit). Validate only schema fields appear in results and unsupported filters are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create several configuration records with unique keys, values, and descriptions to provide data for filtering and pagination scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a configuration by id. First, create a configuration via POST /discussionboard/configurations to obtain a valid id. Retrieve the configuration by id and validate all fields match. Attempt to fetch a configuration with an invalid UUID format and confirm error handling. Then attempt with a well-formed but nonexistent UUID and ensure a 404 not found error is returned. Confirm only schema-defined fields are included in outputs, and that no extra fields are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain a valid configuration id to test successful retrieval and to distinguish behavior with an existing id versus invalid or missing id.

scenario.draft: Test updating a configuration record. Begin by creating two configuration records with unique keys using POST /discussionboard/configurations. Update one record by id (acquired from creation response) and validate all allowed fields have changed. Attempt to update with a key that already exists in another config and expect a unique constraint error. Try updating a non-existent id and validate a 404 error. Also attempt updates that reference fields not present in schema and ensure proper schema validation errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple configuration records to test valid update, uniqueness violation, and prepare for non-existent id and invalid field scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test hard-deleting a configuration record. Create a configuration via POST /discussionboard/configurations to receive a valid id. Delete the record and verify it no longer appears in listings (PATCH). Attempt to delete again and confirm proper 404 error response for already-deleted or non-existent ids. Confirm response returns no body and correct status code as described in the API. Attempt deletion with an invalid or malformed UUID to check error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Provide a configuration to delete and test deletion scenarios including not found and malformed id cases.
Verify that the configuration has been deleted by confirming absence in the configuration listing after deletion.

scenario.draft: Test creating a system notification log. Prepare valid input with target_id as a valid or null UUID, supply type, title, body (optional), and delivered flag. Confirm response contains system-managed fields and accurate data. Attempt to create a notification with missing required fields, an invalid (malformed) UUID for target_id, or extra unsupported fields—expect validation errors and proper error messages. Also test unique constraints/foreign-key error if referencing invalid target ids, following schema rules.

Test the ability for a member to search and paginate through threads using multiple filters, such as by board ID, author member ID, date range, and by partial keyword in the title or body. Ensure that only threads with non-null deleted_at are excluded. Verify response includes correct pagination data and filtered thread records. Set up data by creating multiple boards, members, and threads with different attributes, some of which are soft-deleted (deleted_at set).

dependencies.purpose: Create boards to enable filtering of threads by different boards.
Create member accounts to be used as thread authors.
Create multiple threads with diverse authors and boards, including both active and soft-deleted ones.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a specific thread's details by its UUID. Validate the response returns all required schema fields for a valid thread, and omits soft-deleted threads (where deleted_at is set). Attempt to fetch with: (1) a valid existing thread ID, (2) a thread that is soft-deleted, and (3) a non-existent or incorrectly formatted UUID. Ensure appropriate error handling or null responses in each case.

dependencies.purpose: Create threads for testing normal fetch and soft deleted fetch scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test updating a thread's title and body. Cover cases where: (1) the update is performed by the original author with valid data, (2) an attempt is made with invalid data (e.g., empty title, invalid body format), and (3) an attempt is made to update a soft-deleted thread. Ensure system returns validation errors or not found as appropriate and disables editing of deleted threads.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to test updating operations for both valid and invalid scenarios.
Soft-delete the thread to test editing behavior on deleted resources.

Confirm required fields (assigned_at, optional expires_at/revoked_at) work as described by the schema and the role assignment can be queried post-creation. Ensure uniqueness constraint for member_id is enforced – only one active moderator assignment is allowed per member.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be assigned as a moderator.
Assign admin role to another member, so there is an authorized admin who can perform the assignment.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a moderator assignment for a member who is already a moderator, expecting a uniqueness constraint violation and proper error response. Ensure that the system prevents double assignment for the same member as moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member and assign the moderator role using the POST /discussionboard/moderators endpoint.
Assign an admin role to enable the requestor to make the moderator assignment.

scenario.draft: Test listing administrator assignments using different combinations of filters such as member_id, assigned_by_admin_id, assigned_at, and revoked_at. The scenario should validate that only admin users are authorized, all filter fields exist in the schema, and response results are properly paginated. Include a case where results should include both active and revoked assignments by setting/retrieving revoked_at accordingly. Also test pagination and sorting, ensuring returned results match query filters exactly.

dependencies.purpose: To create both an administrator and a target member for assignment.
Assign an admin role to a member, establishing different test assignments with varying revoked_at and assigned_at for filter testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a specific administrator assignment by id as an authorized admin. First, create a member and assign admin privileges. Use the returned id to fetch the assignment and verify correct retrieval with all schema-defined fields present. Then, attempt to retrieve an assignment using a non-existent or invalid id and confirm that the system responds with an informative error message or not found result. Covers both success and error retrieval cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user to serve as the admin assignee.
Assign administrator role to member; obtain resulting assignment id for test.

scenario.draft: Test updating administrator assignment by id, covering scenarios including normal field updates (where permitted) and revoking admin status via the revoked_at field. Validate that only permissible schema fields are accepted, reject updates to immutable fields, and confirm that updates are not possible for non-existent records. Also verify updating a record already revoked (revoked_at set) by attempting allowed edits and ensuring correct error or inactive state is maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Provision both an admin (to perform the update) and a target member for admin assignment.
Assign admin role to member and obtain assignment id for update.

scenario.draft: Test soft-revoking an administrator assignment by id. First, assign an admin role to a member and delete (set revoked_at) the assignment, validating that admin rights are lost and the revoked_at field is timestamped. Retest by deleting the same id to confirm idempotency (operation is safe if already revoked). Include a negative test where an invalid or non-existent id is provided and the system responds with a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and an admin for the action.
Assign admin role to member to generate an active admin assignment.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new channel with all required schema-defined fields (code, name, description, position, active) as an admin. Validate business rules by first creating a channel with unique code and name (success) and then attempting to create a second channel with a duplicate code and/or name (expecting uniqueness constraint violation error). Also test with invalid values or missing required attributes and verify that validation errors are returned for each failure case.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be assigned as an admin.
Assign admin privileges used to authorize the channel creation requests.

scenario.draft: Test searching and paginating the list of moderation report types using various filter combinations. Create several report types with different code, display_name, description, active status, and created_at values. Request the list with filters set for specific status (active/inactive), creation date range, partial or full matches on code or display_name, and test pagination by limiting result set size and requesting different pages. Validate that only report types matching the filter conditions are returned. Test edge cases—empty results for no matching filters, single result, and full-page result. Ensure invalid filter parameters are rejected with errors, not ignored or returning all records.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple distinct report types to provide comprehensive data for list filtering and pagination scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a specific moderation report type by its unique id. First, create a report type, then fetch its details using the returned id and validate that all schema fields are present and correct. Attempt to fetch a report type using a random/invalid UUID and verify that the system returns a not found error. Test access control to ensure only admins can retrieve report type details as per authorization requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create a report type to ensure a valid id is available for fetch and validation scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test updating a moderation report type identified by its id. Create two report types first: type A and type B. Try updating type A's fields (code, display_name, description, active) and verify the changes persist. Then attempt to update type A's code to duplicate type B's code and verify the API returns a uniqueness violation error. Also, test invalid update attempts: updating non-existent fields, providing an invalid id, and setting code/display_name to empty or unacceptable values. Include scenarios for re-activating/deactivating a report type.

dependencies.purpose: Create two report types so uniqueness and update scenarios can be tested reliably.

scenario.draft: Test the deletion of a moderation report type by id. First, create a report type, then delete it and verify it is no longer retrievable. Attempt to delete a report type using an invalid/non-existent id and verify a suitable not found error. If the report type is referenced by existing reports, attempt deletion and confirm the correct foreign key constraint error or cascading behavior occurs. Test that only admins can perform deletion as per the authorization policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a report type solely for the purposes of deletion and edge-case testing.
Create a report type, then assign it to a report using the report creation API to create a reference for foreign key constraint testing.
Link a report to a report type to validate foreign key restriction or cascading behavior on delete.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a moderation action with all required fields. Prepare prerequisite records: acting moderator (admin or moderator member), report (optional), and a target object (post, comment, or member). Attempt creating a moderation action with each target type, supplying rationale, action_type (such as delete, warn), and the timestamp. Validate successful creation returns all required schema fields. Next, try with invalid actor/target/report references or missing required fields, and verify that appropriate errors are returned. Test edge case where report_id is omitted vs. provided, and business logic cases such as banning or warning a user (ensure correct association in resulting record).

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account with administrator or moderator role for acting_moderator_id reference.
Create a target object (post) for target_object_type='post' moderation action scenario.
Create a moderation report type to be referenced by a report for testing report_id link.
Create a report associated with the target object and acting moderator, to be used as report_id for moderation action creation.

scenario.draft: Test searching and listing discussion board posts using multiple filters (e.g., by thread ID, member ID, board ID, title keyword, is_deleted flag) and combinations thereof. Scenario should validate that correct posts are returned matching all filter parameters, and pagination returns only the expected page of results according to page size and offset settings. Should include at least one test where is_deleted=true to ensure deleted posts can be filtered for moderation/audit. Business context: administrators and users may need to see either active or deleted posts for reporting, analytics, or moderation. Also test for no-results scenario (filters matching nothing).

dependencies.purpose: Register test members to use as authors of posts and owners of related entities.
Create one or more threads to associate posts with for searching by thread ID.
Create several posts with varying fields (different thread IDs, member IDs, board IDs, titles, is_deleted) to seed search/filter scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a discussion board post by its unique ID when the post exists and is not deleted. Confirm that all schema fields are returned and values match what was created, including references to thread and member. Sensitive or unauthorized fields must not be exposed. Business relevance: provides detail views for members and moderation workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to ensure a valid discussionboard_member_id for post creation.
Create a thread to associate with the post being retrieved.
Create the post and obtain its ID for subsequent GET detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test error response when retrieving a discussion board post with an ID that does not exist. Confirm that a 404 error or appropriate error object is returned. This situation may occur if a user tries to access a deleted or invalid post. The system should not leak any internal information. Business rule covers both client bugs and links to deleted/missing content.

Test behavior when retrieving a post that exists but has is_deleted flag set to true (soft deleted). Validate that the post's data is still retrievable for moderation or audit (if business logic allows) or that an appropriate not found/null/hidden response is returned if the policy is to conceal deleted content in detail view. Business context: supports moderation, user appeals, and audit needs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as author of the post to be soft deleted.
Create a thread for the post.
Create the post for deletion and retrieval.
Soft-delete the created post by setting is_deleted=true before fetching.

scenario.draft: Validate updating a post's title and body by the original author. Ensure updated fields are reflected and other fields remain unchanged. Proper permissions should be checked, ensuring only the author (or user with proper rights) can edit. Business value: members edit/correct their posts, fix typos, or add details post-publication. Changes should be audit-logged via post details or snapshots.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to act as the author editing the post.
Create the thread for association.
Create the original post to later update.

scenario.draft: Update attempt for a post with an invalid or nonexistent ID. Validate proper 404 or error response and that no posts are changed. This covers the business rule of not silently failing or corrupting data when an edit is attempted on removed/missing content.

Attempt to update a post using a member who is not the original author (and not admin/moderator). Ensure update is denied and error is returned. Check that post fields remain unchanged. This supports business rules for post ownership and prevents unauthorized user modification.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members: one as the author, one as the unauthorized user.
Create the thread to be used for the post.
Create the post as the first member (author).

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a post that has been previously soft deleted (is_deleted=true). Validate whether updates are allowed (if business logic restricts editing deleted content, expect a suitable error), or if allowed, verify modification is reflected correctly. This tests audit and moderation constraints and supports appeals/history workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post author for the test case.
Create related thread.
Create the post to soft delete and update.
Soft-delete the post prior to attempting update.

scenario.draft: Soft delete a post (set is_deleted=true) as the author. Ensure response confirms deletion and that the post is no longer visible in standard list/search, but is retrievable for audit/moderation if business logic allows. Check that repeated delete requests for the same ID are idempotent or return appropriate status. Covers accidental/malicious deletion and user controls for self-managed content.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to act as author of the post.
Create a thread for association.
Create the post to be soft deleted.

scenario.draft: Attempt to soft delete a post by a member who is not the author and does not have elevated permissions. Confirm the post is not deleted and an error is returned. This enforces business logic restricting deletion to authorized users and supports content integrity and auditability.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members (one author, one non-author) for the roles in this scenario.
Create the thread to be used for the post.
Create the original post as the author.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a post using an invalid or nonexistent post ID. Validate appropriate error response (404 or custom error) and no changes in system state. This scenario supports robustness against client-side errors and malicious guessing of identifiers.

When a post is edited, a snapshot should be created to record its previous state. Test creating a post snapshot that references the edited post, includes the expected title/body/editor_member_id, and sets the correct taken_at timestamp. Validate that the returned snapshot matches input data and system audit policies. This supports rollback, audit, and compliance workflows for content history.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will edit and snapshot the post.
Create a thread for the post.
Create the post needing its state snapshotted before edit.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a post snapshot with a discussionboard_post_id that does not correspond to any existing post. Confirm that a suitable error is returned and that no snapshot is created. This guards against audit history corruption and client validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a plausible editor_member_id for the failed reference scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully search and paginate settings by providing valid filters such as scope_type (e.g., channel, section), key, and value. Create several unique settings first (using POST /discussionboard/settings), each with distinct scope_type, key, value, and description. Use the PATCH /discussionboard/settings endpoint to filter and page through settings, confirming that the returned results match the provided filters and respect pagination controls.

dependencies.purpose: Create several settings entries in the system with varying scope_type, key, value, and description. This ensures there are sufficient and variable records to test the filter and pagination logic thoroughly.

scenario.draft: Test that searching with invalid filter fields (fields not in the schema or incorrect field names) returns a validation or error response. Attempt to submit a filter request to PATCH /discussionboard/settings with fields that are not part of the schema, and confirm that the system rejects the request with a meaningful error indicating invalid filter parameters.

Verify that an admin can retrieve the details of an existing settings record by its id. First, create a setting using POST /discussionboard/settings. Then, use GET /discussionboard/settings/{id} with the returned id and ensure the correct details are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a unique settings entry so its id can be used for retrieval with GET /discussionboard/settings/{id}.

scenario.draft: Test that querying a settings record with a nonexistent id returns a not found error. Use a randomly generated UUID that does not correspond to any existing settings entry in the GET /discussionboard/settings/{id} request and verify the system returns the appropriate error.

Test successful updating of a settings record when valid fields and values are provided. First, create a setting via POST /discussionboard/settings. Then, update mutable fields such as value or description with PUT /discussionboard/settings/{id}, confirming the system applies the updates and returns the modified record.

dependencies.purpose: Create a settings record that can be immediately updated in the test.

scenario.draft: Ensure the system rejects an update attempt if changing a setting's key to a value that already exists in another setting, thereby violating the unique constraint. Create two distinct settings with unique keys, then attempt to update one to the other’s key using PUT /discussionboard/settings/{id} and confirm a unique constraint violation error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first unique settings entry to establish a key that will be duplicated.
Create a second settings entry with a different key, which will be used to attempt a duplicate update against the first.

scenario.draft: Test that trying to update a setting using a UUID that does not match any existing record triggers a not found error. Generate a random UUID with no corresponding entry and perform a PUT /discussionboard/settings/{id} request, checking for the appropriate error response.

Verify the ability to permanently delete a settings record. Create a setting via POST /discussionboard/settings, then delete it with DELETE /discussionboard/settings/{id} using its id. Confirm the deletion is successful, and the record cannot be retrieved afterward.

dependencies.purpose: Create a settings entry that can be deleted during the test.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to delete a settings record using a non-existent id results in a not found error. Issue DELETE /discussionboard/settings/{id} with a UUID that does not correspond to any record and verify that the system returns the expected error message.

Test the ability of an admin to create a new board with valid required fields (discussionboard_board_category_id, discussionboard_section_id, name, and code) and optional fields (description, is_active, is_visible). First, ensure that valid category and section records exist, then create a board using POST /discussionboard/boards and verify the response includes the new board data as specified.

Create a section to satisfy the discussionboard_section_id foreign key requirement when creating a board.

scenario.draft: Ensure that board creation fails when attempting to use a code that already exists for another board, thereby violating the unique constraint. First, create a board with a specific code, then attempt to create another board (with a different name) using the same code, and verify the system returns a unique constraint error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board category for the first and second board.
Create a section for the first and second board.
Create the initial board with a specific code to set up the duplicate scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that creating a board with invalid or nonexistent foreign key references (such as a category or section id that does not exist) results in a foreign key violation error. Attempt to create a board using randomly generated UUIDs for category and section ids and confirm the system rejects the request with an appropriate error.

Test that board creation is rejected if any required fields (such as discussionboard_board_category_id, discussionboard_section_id, name, or code) are omitted. Attempt to create a board missing one or more required fields and confirm the system returns field validation errors.

Test the ability to search and retrieve bans using different filtering criteria such as by banned member, acting moderator, report association, ban type (temporary/permanent), and date ranges. Validate correct results are returned according to the supplied filters, including correct pagination behavior. First, create valid members (both banned and moderator roles), then create at least one report record, and then create multiple bans reflecting each filter scenario to verify correct search response. Attempt searches that should return zero, one, or multiple results. Confirm only schema-defined fields are used for filtering and results.

Use to create ban records with various combinations of fields (ban_type, report_id, etc.) to test all filtering and pagination cases.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a specific ban by its unique ID. Validate successful fetching when using a valid existing ID, and confirm that a not-found (404) error is returned for a non-existent or incorrectly formatted ID. The returned record must contain only schema-defined fields. Ensure permission and access controls are enforced for moderator/admin roles. Set up a valid ban record prior to retrieval, then attempt to fetch with a random/nonexistent ID for failure case.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be banned.
Create a member with moderator privileges to use as acting_moderator_id.
Create a ban for retrieval testing.

scenario.draft: Test updating a ban record by id, modifying different schema-defined fields such as reason, ban_type, expires_at, and referencing a different report or moderator if needed. Verify correct update on valid data and that errors occur for not found, invalid UUIDs, or attempts to set fields not in the schema. After setup, update both mutable and immutable fields to confirm only allowed updates are processed. Also, test update of an expired ban. Attempt updates with invalid data types or references to check for correct error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create original banned member for the starting ban record.
Create moderator member (acting_moderator_id).
Create a ban for updating.

scenario.draft: Test permanent deletion of a ban record by id. Confirm successful deletion for a valid id, and that a not-found error is returned for already-deleted or never-existent IDs. Ensure permission model is enforced, and once a record is deleted, retrieval attempts return not found. Verify the operation works only for users with moderator/admin roles. Sequence: create member, moderator, then ban, delete it by id, and attempt to fetch to confirm deletion. Test deletion of non-existent id as well.

dependencies.purpose: Create a banned member.
Create a moderator member.
Create a ban to test deletion.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a warning record for a member. Create scenarios with both valid and invalid data: (1) Issue a warning with all required schema fields using an existing member and acting moderator, (2) attempt to create a warning for a non-existent member, (3) try invalid report_id or missing required fields and verify validation errors, (4) confirm that business rules for moderation escalation (e.g., more than three warnings) are accounted for in the system if enforced. Create required related resources first; attempt duplicate or conflicting creation for constraint checks.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member who will receive the warning (warned_member_id).

Create a report record to associate with the warning for moderation tracking.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving details of a single moderation report using both a valid report ID and various invalid (non-existent or malformed UUID) IDs. For the valid ID, ensure all schema fields (including report type, reporter, target object type, and description) are present and data matches what was originally created. For invalid or missing IDs, verify that the endpoint returns appropriate errors or not found responses. Confirm that only moderator/admin users can access report details, and access is denied or errors given to unauthorized roles or unauthenticated users.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for the reporting member.

scenario.draft: Test updating mutable fields of a report, such as changing the report description or report type, with both valid and invalid data. Scenario includes: (1) successful update by a moderator or admin, (2) attempt to update an immutable field or set invalid report type values, (3) updating with a non-existent report ID. Ensure proper error messages for violations of data constraints and permissions, and that only permitted fields are updated without impacting immutable columns. Confirm audit-able behavior and integrity of the updated report entity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a reporting member account whose report can be updated.
Create multiple report types to test changing the type in an update.
Create a report to be updated in the test.

scenario.draft: Test permanently deleting a moderation report with both a valid ID and with invalid/non-existent IDs. Confirm that successful deletion removes the record so that subsequent GET/PUT requests for the report return not found or appropriate responses. Test that only authorized moderator/admin users can perform this operation – attempt deletion with insufficient permissions (regular members, unauthenticated), expecting access denied errors. Also confirm deletion is irreversible, and no soft-delete recovery is possible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a reporting member and a moderator/admin user who will attempt deletion.
Create a report type for the test report.
Create a report that will be deleted in the test.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new report type with valid data, ensuring all required schema fields (code, display_name, description, active flag) are handled correctly, and the created record matches expectations. Then attempt to create another report type with duplicate code or display_name values to verify that uniqueness constraints are enforced and proper errors are returned. Also, try creating a report type with missing required fields to validate input validation logic. Confirm that only admin roles can invoke this endpoint and unauthorized attempts are denied.

Test that a member can search and list comments using various schema-allowed filters such as post, member, content substring, and apply pagination controls (offset/limit). Prepare data by creating at least two posts and several comments by different members. Verify that filters narrow results correctly and only schema-defined fields are accepted. Confirm paginated results include correct objects and metadata.

Create several comments associated with test posts and different members.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a comment by its id when it exists and has not been soft deleted. Create a member and a post, then add a comment. Confirm fetching by id returns the correct data with all schema fields.

Create the comment to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test changing a comment’s parent_id to convert it into a reply to another comment. Create two comments, then update one with the other's id as its parent_id. Check the reply relationship is established and object reflects only schema changes.

Soft-delete the comment to simulate update on deleted comment.

Add a comment for delete test.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for comment.
Add and soft-delete a comment.

scenario.draft: Test successful member registration by providing a unique username, a unique email address, a valid hashed_password, a supported role value, and is_active=true. The test should verify that the system creates the member, omits sensitive fields from the response, and populates auto-generated fields (id, created_at, updated_at) while rejecting any unauthorized request to submit such fields. It should confirm the user can log in (if integrated) and that the assigned role matches allowed enums. This scenario confirms the system’s normal registration workflow.

Attempt to create a new member using a username that already exists in the system while supplying all other valid fields. This test should first register a member, then attempt another registration using the same username but a different email. The expected outcome is a failure due to the unique username constraint, and the system should return an appropriate error indicating the violation, without creating a new member.

dependencies.purpose: First create a member record with the target username to set up the duplicate constraint situation.

dependencies.purpose: Register the initial member using the target email address to establish the duplicate constraint for the following test.

Confirm no new member is created and the error response cites the invalid role value.

Verify that omitting required fields (such as username or email) from the registration request results in validation failure. Attempt creating a member with each required field missing in turn. The system should refuse the request, provide clear error messages for missing fields, and not create any user record.

Test searching for registered members using combined filters on username and email fields. Ensure only members matching the given criteria are returned, and confirm pagination, sorting, and exact filtering respect the provided schema field constraints. At least one member should be created beforehand to guarantee a match.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more members that can be later searched by username/email for a positive match scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that filtering on the 'role' field returns only members assigned a specific role. Confirm the role filter excludes members with other roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create members with various role assignments (using valid role enums) to enable meaningful role-based search filtering.

scenario.draft: Check that querying with a date range on created_at returns only those members created within the specified window. The scenario should involve creating members at known timestamps and then search using from/to filters to verify correct inclusion/exclusion. The result must match the specified range, and pagination should operate as expected.

scenario.draft: Attempt to filter using a non-existent field (e.g., 'deleted_at', which is not part of the schema) and ensure that the system rejects the query, returning a validation error that only schema-defined fields are permitted.

Retrieve an existing member by their valid id and ensure all returned fields match the schema (omitting hashed_password). The member must be created first, then fetched by the returned id. Check that all fields exist as described, and verify response structure does not contain sensitive or non-schema fields. Confirm the member is not soft/hard deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member, extract their id for subsequent retrieval in the test scenario.

Try to fetch a member using a well-formed but nonexistent UUID. Confirm that the system correctly returns a not found error and does not reveal sensitive or extraneous error details.

Update specific fields (such as username, email, or role) on an existing member record. First, create a member, collect their id, then change one or more updatable fields with valid values. dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be updated by id in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Try to update a member using a well-formed but non-existent UUID as id. Supply all other fields valid, and expect the service to return a not-found error, assuring no accidental data creation or modification occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to be used for soft-deletion.
